observation.visible_scene: Extreme close-up of a bearded man's face in bright side sunlight, against a pale paneled wall. A black ribbed suction-cup device mounted on a metal shaft is pressed to his right cheek (frame-left), gripping and drawing a patch of cheek skin inward into a puckered dimple. His eyes stay wide open throughout. The framing is essentially locked on the lower face; the device and shaft shift only slightly at the left edge.
visible_changes: The suction device holds its grip on the cheek for the whole excerpt, keeping a dimple of pulled skin around the cup; the cheek pull gradually drags the mouth's center a little toward the device side.

The lips change shape continuously: in the early frames they are pursed together with only a small central gap; by the middle frames the mouth opens wider, parting the lips to reveal the upper teeth and gums; in the late frames the mouth rounds into a protruded 'O' / pout with the lower lip pushed forward.

The metal shaft at the left edge appears, disappears, and reappears between frames, indicating small back-and-forth motion of the device or minor framing shifts rather than a single steady translation.

The face itself stays largely in place relative to the frame (nose and eyes keep roughly the same position), so the visible motion is mostly the mouth reshaping and the cheek being held, not a camera pan.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the suction was applied before this excerpt and what releases it after.
What operates or drives the device and the shaft.
Whether the mouth reshaping is voluntary or induced by the cheek pull.
The full extent of the device's travel, since it is partly cropped at the left edge.
uncertain_details: Whether the shaft's appearing/disappearing is device vibration/oscillation or camera shake, given the static background.
The exact cause of the lip 'O' formation (muscle action vs. skin tension from the cup).
Minor vertical framing drift between early and late frames (camera vs. subject movement) is not clearly resolvable.
